name_en: Arame maki — seasonal fish rolled in dried arame seaweed and simmered
summary_ja: 水で戻したアラメ（褐藻の一種）でイワシやサンマを幾重にも巻き、醤油と砂糖で煮付けた鳥羽の郷土料理。伊勢神宮にも献上されてきたアラメを使い、地域によって巻く魚が変わると伝わる。
summary_en: Rehydrated arame, a brown seaweed once offered to Ise Shrine, is wrapped several times around sardine or saury and simmered in soy sauce and sugar. The choice of fish shifts by locality along the Toba coast.
source_title: あらめ巻き 三重県

name_en: Aimaze — julienned vegetables dressed separately then tossed together
summary_ja: 干ししいたけやれんこん、ごぼう、凍りこんにゃくなどをそれぞれ別々に煮て味付けし、合わせ酢で和える料理。法事用の煮しめの残りを刻んで活用したのが始まりとされ、地域で呼び名が変わると伝わる。
summary_en: Dried shiitake, lotus root, burdock, and freeze-dried konjac are each simmered and seasoned separately, then tossed together in a sweetened vinegar dressing. It is said to have begun as a way to use up leftover simmered dishes from funeral gatherings, and the name changes by locality.

name_en: Tofu dengaku — skewered tofu grilled with sweet miso in Iga style
summary_ja: 水切りした豆腐に串を打って焼き、田楽味噌を塗って炙る伊賀地域の料理。魚介の乏しい盆地で貴重なたんぱく源だった豆腐を使い、大晦日や正月、山の口講のもてなしに供されてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Firm tofu is skewered, grilled, brushed with a sweet miso glaze, and grilled again, an Iga-basin dish. In a landlocked area with little access to seafood, tofu was a vital protein source, and the dish was traditionally served at New Year's and mountain-deity rites.
source_title: 豆腐でんがく 三重県

name_en: Garagara oroshi — coarsely grated daikon mixed with dried sardine and miso
summary_ja: 竹製の鬼おろし器で粗くおろした大根に、油揚げやちくわ、煮干し、赤白の味噌、酢を合わせる料理。江戸時代には年貢の代わりに納めた地域もあったとされ、冠婚葬祭や正月の箸休めとして伝わる。
summary_en: Daikon coarsely grated with a bamboo "oni-oroshi" grater is mixed with fried tofu, fish cake, dried sardine, red and white miso, and vinegar. Some areas are said to have once paid it in place of rice tax, and it remains a palate-cleansing side at weddings, funerals, and New Year's.
source_title: ガラガラおろし 三重県

name_en: Kounago no kugini — young sand lance simmered into curled, nail-like strands
summary_ja: 伊勢湾でとれる稚魚コウナゴ（イカナゴ）をザラメと醤油、清酒で煮詰めた佃煮。煮ると細長い身が折れ曲がり、錆びた釘のように見えることが名の由来とされ、春を告げる伊勢湾岸の味と伝わる。
summary_en: Young sand lance from Ise Bay, called kounago locally, are simmered down with coarse sugar, soy sauce, and sake. As the slender fish curl while cooking, they come to resemble rusted nails — the source of the dish's name — and the catch is considered a herald of spring along the bay.
source_title: こうなごのくぎ煮 三重県

name_en: Manbo sumiso ae — lightly boiled ocean sunfish dressed in vinegar-miso
summary_ja: 手で裂いたマンボウの身をさっとゆでて、酢味噌で和える東紀州の料理。長時間煮ると身が縮んでしまうため短時間でゆでるのがこつとされ、鶏のささみに似た歯ごたえが持ち味と伝わる。
summary_en: Ocean sunfish, torn by hand into pieces, is briefly boiled and dressed in vinegar-miso, a dish from the Higashi-Kishu coast. The trick is a short boil, since the flesh shrinks away with prolonged cooking, leaving a texture said to resemble chicken tenderloin.
source_title: まんぼう酢味噌あえ 三重県

name_en: Chatsu — julienned root vegetables simmered in vinegar without soy sauce
summary_ja: 大根や人参、れんこん、昆布、油揚げを千切りにし、酢と砂糖で煮た朝日町の料理。精進料理を盛った朱漆塗りの器「ちゃつ」に由来する名とされ、白く仕上げるため醤油を使わないのが特徴という。
summary_en: Julienned daikon, carrot, lotus root, kelp, and fried tofu are simmered in vinegar and sugar, a dish from Asahi town. Its name is said to come from "chatsu," the red-lacquered vessel once used to serve vegetarian temple food, and soy sauce is deliberately left out to keep the dish pale.

name_en: Rakkasei no nimame — peanuts simmered sweet-savory in place of black beans
summary_ja: 日照時間が長く落花生の栽培に適した東紀州南部や中南勢地域で、殻をむいた落花生をだし汁と砂糖、醤油で柔らかく煮た料理。正月の黒豆の代わりに「まめに暮らせるように」との願いを込めてつくられると伝わる。
summary_en: Shelled peanuts, grown well in the sunny south of Higashi-Kishu and the Chunansei area, are simmered soft in dashi, sugar, and soy sauce. Made in place of black soybeans at New Year's, the dish carries a pun-based wish for a healthy year ahead.
source_title: 落花生の煮豆 三重県
